steps.what: Interpret blueprints, drawings and instructions to establish article specifications
Plan methods and operations for shaping and assembling parts

tasks.design: Retain interpretation and choice of construction methods with the cabinetmaker. Existing {DOCS} drawings support the work, but heterogeneous instructions do not establish a reliable automatic manufacturing specification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Joinery, material behaviour and ambiguous instructions need practical interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: No specific new capability is evidenced for this broad planning task.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling dimensions, repair conditions and feasible assembly order.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise buildability problems before material is cut.
tasks.altitude: Planning judgement and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Construction interpretation and method selection remain craft judgement; no digest was supplied to establish a task-specific saving.

assumptions: Boundary is cabinetmaker interpretation and method choice, excluding physical machining, customer discussion and detailed specification transcription counted elsewhere.
Cabinetmaker produces requirements in s1 with all interpretation and capture time retained. No structured geometry is assumed from oral instructions.
Check native drawing references first. Unchanged planning adds zero upkeep.
research_questions: Which ambiguities require practical judgement before operations can be planned?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=50+50=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Interpretation and construction-method judgement retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define furniture design intent, dimensions and construction constraints
Design furniture geometry using computer-aided drawing software
Check furniture proportions, clearances and buildability before confirming the design

tasks.design: Configure native parametric components in the {OTHER} computer-aided drawing system for repeat furniture families. The cabinetmaker supplies the design brief, adjusts generated geometry and retains aesthetic and buildability decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated furniture geometry is redrawn while dimensions vary.
tasks.enabler_now: Native dimensions, constraints and reusable components can reduce repeated drawing actions without generating design intent.
tasks.still_hard: Novel forms, awkward sites and hardware clearances.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated geometry entry for familiar designs; design authority is unchanged.

reach.learn: Use tolerances and joinery references consistently

evidence.claim: Parametric drawing components are plausible model knowledge; no product case or measured saving is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is cabinetmaker furniture design, excluding customer discussion, machining and separate specification publication. Geometry work overlapping other tasks is allocated once.

Cabinetmaker produces width, height, depth, units, material thickness, construction family and hardware constraints in s1's full 35 hours. Missing dimensions require manual measurement and clarification; no automatic extraction from sketches is assumed.
Test native components before code. Bespoke designs remain manual and no physical fabrication time shrinks.
Four additional focal hours cover component checks and drawing-template maintenance.
research_questions: Do reusable components reduce drawing time after dimension capture and buildability checks?

approvals.approved_version: Exact drawing, dimensions, material, hardware and construction versions; any geometry change voids confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+31.5+20=86.5, gross=13.5, upkeep=4, net=9.5. High assumes repeat furniture families reduce drawing actions by 30%; low retains bespoke drawing effort plus upkeep. Design intent and final checks retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify geometry, machine setup and tooling requirements for programming
Program computers with toolpaths for the verified machining brief
Simulate and verify the program before authorised machine release

tasks.design: Use native toolpath templates and an approved postprocessor in the {OTHER} computer-aided manufacturing system. The cabinetmaker verifies inputs, simulation and release; the generated program cannot start machinery or replace physical setup checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeat machining operations require manual toolpath and program entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native machining templates and postprocessing can generate repeat programs deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Clamping, grain, tool wear and machine-specific setup differences.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise whether the simulated operation matches the real machine and workpiece.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat program entry, with unchanged release and setup responsibilities.

reach.task: Verify setup before running the approved program
reach.learn: Bind geometry and tooling versions to the actual setup

evidence.claim: Native machining templates and postprocessing are plausible model knowledge; no digest validates this shop's program generation or savings.

assumptions: Boundary is cabinetmaker programming and program verification, excluding physical machine setup, operation and first-piece checks; those keep their existing time.

Cabinetmaker produces part/geometry version, units, material, stock size, tool identifiers and dimensions, datum, permitted operations, feeds/speeds and machine/postprocessor version in s1. Its full 35 hours include capture, suitability checks and missing-field reconciliation.
Test native machining templates first. Unsupported geometry, missing tool data or mismatched machine versions require manual programming and verification, never assumed safe defaults.
Six additional focal hours cover template validation and exceptional programs; four specialist hours cover additional postprocessor and machine-profile upkeep.
research_questions: How much manual program entry remains after current native tooling, and does generation save time after simulation and upkeep?

already_counted.description: Machining brief verification and field capture

approvals.approved_version: Exact program checksum, geometry, stock, tools, datum, parameters, machine and postprocessor versions; any change requires renewed verification

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+30=65, gross=35, focal upkeep=6, net=29. High requires a genuine manual repeat-program entry component not already generated by native software. Low retains manual programming for unsupported work plus upkeep. Physical setup, machining and verification do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare detailed specifications and discuss projects

steps.what: Reconcile detailed project specifications with drawings and agreed requirements
Draw up detailed specification sheets from the verified brief
Check the detailed specifications and discuss project choices with customers

tasks.design: Populate approved {DOCS} specification sheets from a cabinetmaker-verified brief. The cabinetmaker checks the sheet before presenting it and retains the full customer discussion; requested changes create a revised version for renewed review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified project details are copied into a separate customer-facing specification.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields and reusable specification templates can remove repeated transcription.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous finishes, exclusions and late customer changes.
tasks.human_edge: Explain choices and recognise mismatches between the specification and customer expectations.
tasks.altitude: Less specification assembly, with unchanged customer contact and design responsibility.

reach.task: Confirm specifications can be built as described
reach.learn: Keep customer-facing detail aligned with shop instructions

evidence.claim: Populating specification templates from verified fields is plausible model knowledge; no measured cabinetmaking case is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is specification reconciliation, sheet assembly and customer discussion, excluding original design and physical construction. Any detailed geometry capture overlapping design tasks is allocated once.

Cabinetmaker produces article IDs, dimensions/units, tolerances, materials, hardware, finishes, quantities, exclusions and drawing versions in s1. Its full 30 hours include capture and ambiguity resolution; no free structured drawing extraction is assumed.
Test native templates first. Missing details return to manual reconciliation; code only copies approved fields and cannot invent finish descriptions.
Five additional focal hours cover template updates and revision exceptions. Customer discussion and customer time remain unchanged.
research_questions: Does template population save assembly time after complete field capture and customer-facing checks?

already_counted.description: Final sheet check and customer discussion

incremental.description: Specification template upkeep and revision exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact specification sheet, drawing versions, dimensions, materials, finishes and exclusions presented to the customer; revisions require renewed check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+0+35=65, gross=35, upkeep=5, net=30. High requires genuine repeat transcription from a verified brief; low retains bespoke assembly and revisions plus upkeep. Requirement reconciliation and customer discussion keep all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeat drawing, program entry and specification assembly may shrink; construction judgement, physical setup and customer discussion remain human.
reach: Bind program versions to setup with CNC tool operators
role.ambitious_version: A cabinetmaker who reuses checked digital components while retaining control of buildability, machining release and customer expectations.
